events.description:

This is the best way to orient to the heart of COhere: building relationships, local knowledge, and a deeper sense of belonging to the place we call home. 

5:30 PM Welcome + tabling from local organizations
6:00 PM Community Dinner (free!!)
6:30 PM COhere Invocation - orientation, teasers, and talks from local leaders
(break)

events.name: Honoring Water | A Guided Morning Practice
events.description: Angelique, a water protector from Commerce City will be joining us in Boulder to guide us in a morning practice to connect with our local waters.

events.name: Phone-Free Friday Social Night
events.description: Phone-Free Friday is a low-key social night at North of Ordinary, a community living room and creative space in Boulder built around real-world connection, creativity, and community. We’re opting out of the scroll, the algorithm, and a culture that demands every spare second of our attention. Instead, we’re putting the phones away and taking the room back. Come alone or bring your crew, grab a drink, work on an art project, play a game, read a book or zine, listen to music, or just talk to people you don’t already know. Join us for a few hours to be present, make things, and just be together. Bring a snack to share if you feel inspired!

events.name: Community Grief Ritual: Tending the Soil
events.description:
Facilitated by Danielle Rifkin, Dan Maynard, and Sarah (Naiya) D'Antoni of the Grief Collective.

Positioned at the opening of Cohere week, this ritual seeds the soil for what the week will grow. Before we can plant connection, we have to grieve where we fractured: where we lost each other, where ruptures went unrepaired, where survival under capitalism pulled us away from each other, where we got severed from land.

We grieve alone because we forgot how to grieve together. This ritual is a return to the village, a remembering that mourning was always meant to be collective.

We'll work with song, story, and systemic constellations, drawing on ritual lineages from Joanna Macy, Francis Weller, Martin Prechtel, Malidoma Somé, and the Mythic Body.

events.name: Mindful Birding Walk at High Plains Environmental Center
events.description:
A mindful birding walk combines traditional birdwatching with mindfulness techniques, focusing on slow-paced, intentional awareness of birds and nature. Observing birds in their natural habitat can be inspiring and relaxing while also offering a variety of health benefits. This way of connecting with nature encourages purposeful curiosity, builds community, and deepens our appreciation for birds and the natural world.

Join us at the High Plains Environmental Center to explore mindfulness and birds and learn simple techniques you can take home and practice on your own. We’ll begin in the
classroom and then head outside for a guided walk.

All abilities and interests are welcome! We'll provide bird books and binoculars.

Please dress appropriately for the weather.
Registration: Sign-up information will be available in September. We will notify registered participants of any changes due to weather or other circumstances.

events.name: Land Noticing Session
events.description: A land noticing session (based on the new Richard Louv book). We’ll meet at the main pavilion for introductions and a grounding exercise, then wander individually out into the park and by the creek to quietly observe the other-than-human kin surrounding us and contemplate our relationship with them. Optional group share after. BYO coffee/tea/water, journal+pen, camera, other art supplies, land offerings (tobacco, healing herbs, stones, etc).

events.name: Resilience Skill Share
Self-Care Serenade
events.description:
Gather your favorite self-care supplies for this cozy collective experience of self-care while being serenaded by live harp!

What is a self-care serenade?

Imagine a cozy, intimate, artsy space filled with live, improvised, meditative music. Your favorite books and self-care supplies are spread around you. You've brought a fluffy pillow and blanket and are finally taking the time to prioritize yourself how we so often are pressured away from doing.

There's a cozy group spread around the room also quietly napping, doing yoga, reading, making art, meditating, and journaling. You've started the evening with a moment to share with each other as much and as little as you each wanted to mention about life, and you're feeling seen. You're not alone in the pressures and injustices of the world, and this room is full of people committed to protecting your right to rest. And you're so grateful they've made this time for themselves too.

Now soft, live music is playing and this time is yours. The whole priority of this event is to have a supported chance to custom-craft a self-care practice that's exactly what your body needs, and exactly what your heart needs too. An hour is set aside ahead of you for being serenaded by improvised harp music without commitments or distractions, with full permission to make this time whatever you need. The music and community and soft lighting all saying "We celebrate you choosing to care for yourself!"

RSVP here: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/boulder-self-care-serenade-october-17th-tickets-1997644153438?aff=oddtdtcreator

events.name: COHere Hub-- Time to Hang, Connect & Create
events.description:
Amidst the many events of COHere, the COhere Hub at the Coffee Stand is a time to slow down and connect with fellow COHere attendees and reflect on what you are noticing, feeling and learning. Stop by, grab a delicious drink or snack, and connect.

As an optional activity to partake in: the upcycled tapestry that is collectively being made throughout COHere will be present and you can contribute to it by answering one of the 4 questions through the making of a patch:

1) what are you/we grieving?
2) what are you/we decomposing?
3) what are you/we building?
4) what are you/we dreaming?

events.description: Boulder and Naropa community member, Angelo will be leading us to get quiet and listen to the land; to resource ourselves, during these challenging times, through being in relationship with the Earth together. events.name: Bindweed School of Agroecology - Community Work Day
events.description:
The Bindweed School of Agroecology works at the intersection of agriculture, ecology, and community, empowering people to take food cultivation and land stewardship into their own hands. Join our team for our regular Sunday workday at our new property in Niwot. We will be doing a collection of seasonal tasks from 10am-1pm, followed by a farm based community lunch (please stay!) Exact activities will be decided closer to the time but may include sheet mulching, moving manure, harvest, food preservation, and/or soap making.

RSVP here: https://form.jotform.com/262704823395159

Email Amy at niwothomestead@gmail.com with any questions, needs, or info on the day's activities.

events.name: Short Film Night: On Place & Belonging
events.description: A curated selection of short, independent films that will explore what shapes our sense of belonging. The films weave in themes of identity, resilience, and our more-than-human kin.

events.name: A Sound Healing Journey into the Womb of the Earth for Ecological Self-Restoration
events.description:
Facilitated by Ayleen Guzman of Mamafaeria Healing Arts

At the center of this offering is the understanding that the Earth is not simply the place where we live, but a living
spiritual presence that can become a gateway into connection with the Divine, the Divine Mother, God, our
ancestors, and ourselves. The womb of the Earth can become a place of return, remembrance, healing, and
transformation.
We are living through profound and rapidly changing times. Across many Indigenous, African, Native, and spiritual
traditions, there are teachings about periods of great transformation in which humanity is called to remember its
relationship with the Earth and return to right relationship with one another. Within my own spiritual framework, this
is a time when the Earth is calling us to become more sensitive to her presence, her needs, and the wisdom she
carries.
The intention of this ceremony is to begin cultivating that relationship consciously.

events.name: People of the Sacred Land: Film Screening + Dialogue
events.description:
The Untold History of Colorado

The idea that we are living on stolen land isn’t new, or even novel; it’s a reality that exists across settler communities worldwide, and many people in the United States are aware of the blatant agendas, coercion, and profound immorality of the treaty process. What’s often missing from that conversation, however, are rigorous, comprehensive, academically supported Native-led studies proving that— even through the lens of modern law— large areas of what we call the United States remain illegally occupied. And nowhere is the evidence and culpability more dramatic than in the state of Colorado. PEOPLE of the SACRED LAND (2026, 32 min) follows Richard Willams (Oglala Lakota, Northern Cheyenne) as he recounts the findings of the Truth, Restoration, and Education Commission (TREC) of Colorado’s TREC Reports. While Rick’s story focuses on Colorado, the approach, implications, and impact of his work provide a model for Native leaders across the continent.

Film will begin at 6 PM. 

Richard Williams: Executive Producer
Dewi: Director, cinematographer, editor
Sarah Ortegon Highwalking: Field director
Jason: Cinematographer, finishing editor

events.name: Growing Gardens Volunteer Shift
events.description:
Growing Gardens offers fall volunteer shifts on our Boulder Farm every Tuesday and Friday.  It is a wonderful opportunity to learn about regenerative agriculture, connect with a local food system, get your hands in the dirt, and create community with others.  

Please register in advance at growinggardens.org/volunteer/ 

There is no prior experience needed to volunteer with Growing Gardens and we provide all necessary equipment and tools. We just ask participants to wear closed-toed shoes, clothing layers, sunscreen or a hat, and to bring a reusable water bottle.

events.name: We can all be more like trees: The forest ecosystem as a model for thriving neighborhoods
events.description: Join us for an interactive workshop where we’ll use the wisdom of the forest to understand what could create a resilient human community.

events.name: Fall Farm Tour and Tea
events.description: Join us for an end-of-season farm tour of our Jewish-community, educational, sustainable farm. We will tour our greenhouse, educational garden, no-till vegetable donation field, and meet the goats. Hear about our many efforts to build the earth's soil and the earth's people. We'll also make herbal tea straight from the garden.

events.description:
Description in progress..
A morning land connection session that will be led by Saoirse Watters, you can find more about her here: https://saoirsewatters.com/

events.name: Social Stitchers Meetup x COHere tapestry curation
events.description:
At the Boulder Library each month all ages of community members come together to crochet, knit, mend, embroider, etc. and make use of communal tools provided by the library. 

At this particular social stitchers gathering, COHere will be inviting folks to contribute to a communal tapestry about Boulder's ecological and communal resilience. Participants will be prompted to make a patch that responds to one of the 4 questions:

1) what are you/we grieving?
2) what are you/we decomposing?
3) what are you/we building
4) and what are you we dreaming?

Embroidery and painting will be ways of decorating patches for the tapestry

location.name: Boulder Public Library-- Boulder Creek Room

events.name: Dinner Table Economics
events.description:
A loving dinner gathering is a map of a healthy economy. It exemplifies everything we need to know so we can build future systems where all are fed and welcome, and it shelters us in care & connection while we do so.

Join food justice advocate and economic systems healer Alex Bernat (they/she) for an approachable exploration of ancestral economic healing, liberatory cooperative models, and radical dreaming as we mobilize in solidarity with San Lazaro as residents secure a future for the neighborhood.

About San Lazaro: https://www.sanlazaroresidents.com/support

More from Alex: https://linktr.ee/alexbernat

This event will take place at the Hawk's Nest, a house that hosts bi-weekly potlucks focused on creativity, community building, storytelling, etc. 

6-7pm: Gathering and mingling
7-8pm: Conversation about Ancestral Economic Healing

events.name: Bad Art Club
events.description: Bad Art Club is North of Ordinary’s signature creative night, where perfectionism comes to die and making things badly is the whole point. North of Ordinary is a community living room and creative space in Boulder built around real-world connection, creativity, and community. This time, we’re making collages. Cut things up, layer them, glue them down, make something strange, political, beautiful, ugly. Bring your own materials or dig through what we’ve got (hello vintage Nat Geos!), and spend time making things alongside other people without worrying about whether the result is “good.” No art experience required. Just scissors, glue, questionable ideas, and a willingness to make a mess.

events.name: Eco-Poetic Writer's Block Jam
events.description:
Join in an eco-poetic exploration this Cohere with one of the best writing communities in town. Writer's Block out of Mi Chantli studio in Boulder is hip, hop, and made for every level and style.

 Tonight you'll get to write, share, and mingle with some of the best. 

No experience necessary. Outside the box all day! 

Your host for this writers Block is Lee Frankel

CreativeMornings Boulder is a free, monthly creative gathering that brings people together to connect, get inspired, and celebrate creativity in all its forms. Through inspiring talks, music, and community, we create an inclusive space where people from all backgrounds can share ideas, find inspiration, and build connections. events.name: Caring for families who care for families
events.description:
"It takes a village" ... a common refrain we hear from parents and those supporting families. But what does it take to cultivate this sense of collective care in a village, or to create said village?

This event is a meet and greet for families and those feeling called to support families in a deeper way. We will get to know one another, share our dreams, challenges, and needs...and enjoy the time outside while little ones run around the park (with support!).

Who knows, you might even meet people you want to start a daycare share with, or another family to try co-living with!

events.name: Uprooting Qahr! Power, Privilege, and Paperwork
events.description:
Through monologues, film, and live music, Uprooting Qahr! Power, Privilege, and Paperwork, follows Taishya Adams - educator, artist, and policymaker - as she shares personal and political narratives that confront the colonial cancer that spread from Europe to Africa, the Americas and West Asia. Weaving across time and space, we face the uneven promise of democracy and the possibilities of liberty and justice for all.  

Registration: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeJuMVFgHlvcUPKhqoQqf7APPiPpwdW2YCT_4PyLd67YvYFdQ/viewform
